hook: SCP-3866 is a batch of unlabeled pills that put a person into a deep hibernation, with one heartbeat every thirty-four days, that might last thousands of years. They turned up at an amateur clinic selling assisted suicide, which the Foundation investigated during an end-of-death scenario. The file is short, and a good chunk of it is a text exchange with a supplier called dado, whose broken spelling is the comic centre of the piece. Pay attention to what the clinic staff did with each patient after the pill took effect.
whyItMatters:
This is a compact piece that pairs a slapstick middleman with a quietly awful premise. The comedy and the horror sit side by side rather than one undercutting the other.

It also shows how a world-scale scenario changes the meaning of small, mundane crimes. A euthanasia clinic would normally be a matter for police, but here the Foundation has to decide whether it is a scam, an anomaly, or both, and the answer turns out to be both.
thingsToNotice:
The clinic never killed anyone; it buried its sleeping patients behind the building, 541 in all and 491 of them without a casket. In July, civilians report screaming, weeping and retching from the ground, and the Foundation digs them up, scrubs the soil, minerals and insects out of their bodies, gives them amnestics and sends them home with cover stories.

Read dado's texts again with that ending in mind. He offers the longest sleep, says his test hamster is still asleep, worries about delivering on foot in the rain, and the meeting address leads only to an apartment holding a phone, half a donut, three empty Amazon boxes and a mattress.
